n:De La Rue: De La Rue is a banknote printer based in Basingstoke, United Kingdom, tied to 38 central banks. It prints or supplies notes for most of them. The Bank of England awarded it a 500 million pound printing contract on 29 September 2014, worked at the Bank's Debden site in Essex, and later triggered a three-year extension of its polymer banknote contract to 2028. The Central Bank of Kenya gave it an 18 billion shilling contract for new-look currency, made at the Ruaraka plant it co-owns with the Kenyan government, ahead of Giesecke & Devrient, Crane Currency and Oberthur Fiduciaire; Crane AB disputed that award before the procurement review board. Sveriges Riksbank signed with it on 19 September 2018 for just over three years, replacing Crane, and Danmarks Nationalbank has signed for the new Danish series launching in 2028, for a minimum of six years. The National Bank of Ethiopia gave it 187 million birr of a 206 million birr deal, for the 100 birr note, and the national bank of North Macedonia three contracts for 45 million notes worth 3.775 million euros. Printing or supply is also recorded for Libya, South Sudan, Tanzania, Ghana, Albania, Lesotho, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, the Gambia, Namibia, Botswana, Seychelles, Mauritius, Cape Verde, Iceland, Fiji, Tonga, the Maldives, Bhutan, Jamaica, Belize, Barbados, Trinidad and Tobago, Bermuda, the Cayman Islands, the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, Bahrain, Qatar, Turkmenistan and Iraq. Two records concern conduct. A United Nations Human Rights Council commission report said the firm transferred about 1.4 million dollars between 2016 and September 2017 to a Nairobi account held by a Bank of South Sudan consultant, against a banknote contract worth about 144 million dollars, and noted 'suspected corruption'; the United Kingdom's Serious Fraud Office opened an investigation in July 2019 and closed it in June 2020, saying the case did not meet the test for prosecution. In September 2010 De La Rue said some employees had deliberately falsified banknote paper specification test certificates for a limited number of customers, which was followed by the suspension of supply to the Reserve Bank of India. At the trial of former Central Bank of Nigeria governor Godwin Emefiele over the alleged unlawful printing of redesigned naira notes in 2022, an allegation that is unproven, a prosecution witness said original naira designs had historically been handled by De La Rue while the new notes were printed locally.
n:International Monetary Fund: The International Monetary Fund is an international lender based in Washington, United States, tied to 30 central banks and one other body. Most of those ties are careers rather than conduct: former Fund staff and officials have gone on to run or help run central banks in Kenya (Kamau Thugge and Patrick Njoroge), Mexico (Agustín Carstens, a former deputy managing director of the Fund, and Guillermo Ortiz), Pakistan (Reza Baqir, once chief of its Debt Policy Division), India (Raghuram Rajan, its former chief economist, and deputy governor Urjit Patel), Israel (Stanley Fischer, Jacob Frenkel and Karnit Flug), Bangladesh (Ahsan H Mansur), Mozambique, the Netherlands, Brazil, South Korea, Sweden, Malaysia, Colombia, Zambia, Trinidad and Tobago, Uruguay, Georgia, Costa Rica, Botswana, Suriname, North Macedonia, Madagascar, Curaçao, the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank and the Central Bank of West African States, and two Federal Reserve figures, Frederic S. Mishkin and Angel Ubide, also worked with the Fund. It sits on the Financial Stability Board, a body of regulators and central banks, represented by first deputy managing director Dan Katz. Four records concern money and reporting. In May 2023, an election year, Argentina's central bank passed a further 140 billion pesos to the Treasury as temporary advances, taking transfers since March to 370 billion pesos and using 99.2 per cent of the 372.8 billion peso first-half limit agreed with the Fund. The Bank of Ghana said in February 2023 that its claims on the government at December 2022 included a 37.9 billion cedi overdraft to cover auction shortfalls and maturing bonds, 7.2 billion cedis of treasury bonds bought from banks and 8.9 billion cedis of on-lent Fund money, after the government, the bank and the Fund had earlier adopted zero deficit financing. In December 2021 Malawi police arrested Kabambe and Mwanamvekha, saying they had procured and masterminded the falsification of reserve returns to make the Fund believe Malawi was meeting the conditions of its Extended Credit Facility; that allegation is unproven. In March 2008 the Fund's Executive Board found that the National Bank of Tajikistan had supplied inaccurate information on the cotton sector, international reserves, net domestic assets and credit policy, including reporting reserves of about 450 million dollars when they were roughly a third of that and concealing that reserves were pledged as collateral for loans to the cotton sector, and Tajikistan was required to repay 47.4 million dollars.
n:Note Printing Australia: Note Printing Australia prints banknotes at Craigieburn in Victoria, Australia, is wholly owned by the Reserve Bank of Australia and is tied to 20 central banks. In 2006/07 it produced 245 million notes for the Reserve Bank itself and filled export orders for the central banks of Chile, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Brunei, Singapore and New Zealand; its customer list adds polymer notes produced and supplied for the central banks of Romania, Mexico, the Philippines, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Thailand, Kuwait, Samoa, the Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Vanuatu and Vietnam. Three of those relationships carry a criminal case. In October 2011 Note Printing Australia and Securency, a joint venture half owned by the Reserve Bank, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to foreign public officials in order to win banknote business from the note-issuing authorities of Indonesia (December 1999 to February 2001), Malaysia (October 2001 to December 2003), Nepal (February 2000 to May 2002) and Vietnam. The officials are not named. Securency paid 19,809,772 Australian dollars and Note Printing Australia 1,856,710 Australian dollars in proceeds-of-crime penalties, with fines of 480,000 and 450,000 Australian dollars; Securency's former chief financial officer received a suspended six-month sentence for false accounting in 2012 and its agent Radius Christanto a suspended two-year sentence in 2013. After the 2011 charges the Reserve Bank's board set up a special committee and commissioned an independent governance review by Cameron Ralph. Separately, a former Bank Negara Malaysia official, Mohamad Daud, was charged in July 2011 with receiving two bribes of 50,000 ringgit each in 2004 and 2005 linked to a 95 million ringgit contract for 5 ringgit polymer notes won by Note Printing Australia; the Shah Alam Sessions Court acquitted him on 6 December 2015 without calling his defence, and the Attorney-General withdrew the appeal in February 2016.
n:Oberthur Fiduciaire: Oberthur Fiduciaire is a banknote printer based in Paris, France, tied to 13 central banks, for which it prints or supplies notes. Danmarks Nationalbank chose it as its new banknote supplier under a four-year framework, with the first notes in circulation in 2020. In Germany it won a Deutsche Bundesbank tender to print part of the euro notes for 2013, after an earlier award about two years before that losing bidders had challenged without success; the Bundesbank's tender for 2012 gave it 526 million 10-euro notes. The Banco Central de Bolivia awarded it an international tender on 27 July 2023 worth 25,945,787 US dollars, for 321.5 million notes of 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200 bolivianos. The National Bank of Ethiopia gave it 19.6 million birr of a 206 million birr printing deal, covering the 50 birr note. In North Macedonia the national bank signed a contract, reported on 8 May 2026, to print 100-denar notes for 59,800,000 denars, about 972,358 euros; an earlier contract for the same note, reported in September 2021, had gone to the Russian firm Goznak for about 400,000 euros. The Bank of Uganda's director of currency told a parliamentary committee that the bank's banknote printing contract is with Oberthur, signed on 26 July 2018. The Central Bank of Costa Rica opened a tender in the second half of 2008 for six new denominations and Oberthur won it, printing the 20,000-colon note of 2010 at its plant in Rennes, France. The Bank of the Republic of Haiti ordered a reprint of 30 million 10-gourde notes for 845,000 euros. Single notes or part-series are also recorded in Mauritius (the 25 and 50 rupee notes), Tunisia (the 20-dinar note), Uruguay (the 2,000-peso note of 2015, introduced on 27 April 2016), Burundi (the 2,000-franc note of 11 September 2023) and Bosnia and Herzegovina, where every denomination except the 200 convertible mark note is reported to be printed by the firm.
n:Giesecke+Devrient: Giesecke+Devrient is a banknote printer based in Munich, Germany, tied to 14 central banks. The Central Bank of Kenya disclosed a five-year deal with the firm worth 14.2 billion shillings, or 109,422,740 US dollars, reported on 21 August 2024. The Deutsche Bundesbank's banknote tender for 2012 gave it 526 million 10-euro notes. Asked how it picked the printer for the Central Bank of Armenia's third banknote series, the bank's representative said Giesecke+Devrient 'won as a result of a comprehensive evaluation of all offers'. Single notes or note families are recorded for Eswatini (20 lilangeni), Tajikistan (a commemorative 100 somoni note put into circulation on 30 October 2025), Malawi (2,000 kwacha), Mongolia (5,000 togrog), the Bahamas (1 dollar, introduced on 3 February 2025), Suriname (500 dollars), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (100 and 200 franc notes carrying the firm's Munich imprint), Oman (a commemorative 1 rial polymer note introduced on 11 January 2026), Eritrea (the current nakfa series) and Azerbaijan (the renewed 50 manat note). In Myanmar the customer was the state-owned Security Print Works rather than the central bank: the firm supplied raw materials, supplies and system components for printing kyat banknotes, and said in a release issued in 2021 that it had suspended all deliveries after the military crackdown.
n:KPMG: KPMG is an accounting and auditing firm based in London, United Kingdom, tied to 14 central banks. It audits the accounts of 13 of them. It signed the independent auditors' report on the Federal Reserve Banks' combined financial statements for 2025. It is external auditor of the Bank of Spain for the financial years 2023 to 2027, approved by a European Union Council decision of 19 September 2023. It has audited the Swiss National Bank since 2015, was re-elected by the general meeting of 25 April 2025 and is proposed for 2026 and 2027. It audits the Reserve Bank of Australia, and Note Printing Australia, under a contract with the national audit office, so the Reserve Bank does not choose the audit partner. It also audits the Central Bank of Malta (for 2019 to 2025), the Bank of Ghana (2025), the State Bank of Pakistan (the year ended 30 June 2026, in a report dated 27 August 2026), the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic (statements as at 31 December 2023), the Reserve Bank of Fiji (2022), Banque du Liban in Lebanon (from 2020), the Central Bank of Oman (2023) and the National Bank of Angola (2021). It audited the Bank of England up to the financial year ended 29 February 2024, after which the Bank appointed Ernst and Young. The firm is also named in a Nepalese case. In 2007 Nepal's Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority charged the sitting governor of Nepal Rastra Bank, Bhattarai, and executive director Pradhan with embezzlement over the hiring of American consultants for the second phase of the Financial Sector Reform Program, and Bhattarai was suspended; the Supreme Court later cleared both, allowing his reinstatement, and a confidential World Bank report, reported in 2014, named a private banker as the main figure behind the scandal.
n:EY: EY, also written Ernst & Young, is an accounting and auditing firm based in London, United Kingdom, tied to 13 central banks. It audits the accounts of the Bank of England, where it signed the auditor's report in the 2026 annual report for the year to the end of February 2026, having been appointed from the year ending 28 February 2025; De Nederlandsche Bank in the Netherlands, approved for the financial years 2026 to 2032 by a European Union Council decision of 16 September 2025; the Bank of Canada for 2025, jointly with PricewaterhouseCoopers and appointed by the Governor-in-Council; Norges Bank in Norway for 2022 to 2027, engaged by its supervisory council, with Norway's national audit office also reviewing the oil fund audit; the South African Reserve Bank for 2025/26, jointly with BDO South Africa; the Bank of Cape Verde, where it gave an unqualified opinion for the year ended 31 December 2024 on a balance sheet total of 99,898,332 thousand escudos and negative equity of 622,855 thousand escudos; the Central Bank of Nigeria (2024); the Central Bank of Aruba (2025); the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (2019); and the Central Bank of Yemen, where its appointment was announced on 7 February 2021. Three records go further. In Lebanon, Banque du Liban's 2018 audited accounts, signed off with qualifications by EY and Deloitte, carried a 6.82 billion dollar asset described as 'seigniorage on financial stability', inflating assets by more than 6 billion dollars while the bank helped fund a widening government deficit; the amount was determined each year by the governor. In Tanzania, an Ernst & Young audit of the Bank of Tanzania's External Payment Arrears account found about 133 billion shillings wrongly paid in 2005/06 to 22 local companies, many of them phoney or using fake documents; President Kikwete dismissed governor Ballali in January 2008, companies were ordered to refund the money and some lower-level defendants were jailed. In Portugal, the Bank of Portugal's ethics committee discussed at a meeting in April 2019 a request by governor Carlos Costa to be excused from matters concerning Caixa Geral de Depositos, after an EY audit of that bank's management. Costa had been on its board from 2004 to 2006 and may have sat on extended credit council meetings that approved operations which caused losses, while now heading the supervisor assessing former Caixa directors; vice-governor Elisa Ferreira did not recuse herself but told the committee of a possible conflict of interest relating to her husband's past role at La Seda. The committee's conclusions were not made public.
n:Deloitte: Deloitte is an accounting and auditing firm based in London, United Kingdom, tied to eight central banks. It audits the accounts of the Bank of France for the financial years 2024 to 2029, approved jointly with Mazars by a European Union Council decision of 16 July 2024; the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye, where its Turkish member firm signed the independent auditor's reports on the 2025 financial statements, the bank having used outside auditors since 2000; the Central Bank of Paraguay for 2025, 2026 and 2027, awarded by a board resolution of 7 November 2025 after an international public tender; the Bank of Italy for 2023 to 2027; Bank Al-Maghrib in Morocco, on a six-year non-renewable mandate for 2021 to 2026; and the Central Bank of Libya (2021). Two further records are investigations. In Lebanon, Banque du Liban's 2018 audited accounts, signed off with qualifications by Deloitte and EY, carried a 6.82 billion dollar asset described as 'seigniorage on financial stability', inflating assets by more than 6 billion dollars; the amount was determined each year by the governor. In New Zealand, Deloitte was engaged by the Reserve Bank on 11 March 2016 and reported on 12 April that the leak of the 10 March Official Cash Rate decision came from a Mediaworks employee: a journalist in the bank's media lock-up emailed a draft story out of the room without the bank's approval shortly before 8am, and another employee who overheard colleagues discussing the rate cut emailed Michael Reddell at 8.04am, ahead of the 9am announcement. Reddell did not notify the bank until 9.08am, and Mediaworks reported itself on 5 April 2016. Deloitte judged the Minister of Finance's office unlikely to be the source. The Reserve Bank then ended embargoed lock-ups for news media and analysts.
n:World Bank: The World Bank is an international lender based in Washington, United States, tied to 17 central banks and one other body. Most of the ties are careers, and moving between jobs is not wrongdoing. People have gone from the Bank into central banks: Ishrat Husain to the State Bank of Pakistan; Stanley Fischer, a former chief economist, to the Bank of Israel from 2005 to 2013; Duvvuri Subbarao, a former lead economist, to the Reserve Bank of India from 2008 to 2013; Mario Marcel from a Bank director post to the council of the Central Bank of Chile, approved in September 2015; Hwang Geon-il, a former executive director, to the Bank of Korea's monetary policy committee; Adriana D. Kugler from United States executive director at the World Bank Group to a governorship of the Federal Reserve System, held from 13 September 2023 to 8 August 2025; Mario Draghi from executive director, 1984 to 1990, to the Italian Treasury and later the governorship of the Bank of Italy; Denny Kalyalya to the Bank of Zambia in February 2015; Mamo Mihretu to the National Bank of Ethiopia in January 2023; Marouane Abassi, the Bank's representative in Libya, to the Central Bank of Tunisia, approved by parliament in February 2018; Óscar Évora Santos to the Bank of Cape Verde on 4 January 2021; and B. Lkhagvasuren into the Bank of Mongolia as adviser to the governor in 2000, later its governor, where Enkhjargal Danzanbaljir also moved out to the World Bank and other development banks and back to the supervisory board. Similar moves are recorded at the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank (Sir K Dwight Venner and Timothy N. J. Antoine), the Central Bank of West African States (Jean-Claude Kassi Brou), the Bank of Guyana (Gobind Ganga) and the National Reserve Bank of Tonga (Tatafu Moeaki); Frederic S. Mishkin consulted for the Bank around his time as a Federal Reserve governor. The World Bank also sits on the Financial Stability Board, a body of regulators and central banks, represented by Pablo Saavedra. One record is a case. In 2007 Nepal's Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority charged Nepal Rastra Bank's sitting governor, Bhattarai, and executive director Pradhan with embezzlement over the hiring of American consultants for the second phase of the Financial Sector Reform Program, and Bhattarai was suspended; the Supreme Court later cleared both, and a confidential World Bank report, reported in 2014, named a private banker as the main figure behind the scandal.
n:ABN Amro: ABN Amro is a bank based in Amsterdam, Netherlands, tied to four central banks. Three of the ties are careers. Lord Jitesh Gadhia, a Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court, came from investment banking at Blackstone, Barclays Capital, ABN AMRO and Baring Brothers. Zsigmond Jarai was president and chief executive of ABN-AMRO Bank in Hungary from 1998, after posts at brokerages and banks in London and Budapest, and later led the Magyar Nemzeti Bank; no ethics finding is recorded. Thomas Domhoff took up the presidency of the Centrale Bank van Aruba from 1 July 2026, after project roles at ING, ABN AMRO, Rabobank and Capgemini and a directorship at Banco Sicredi. The fourth tie is a case at the Bank of Italy: on 28 May 2011 a Milan court sentenced former governor Fazio to four years in prison and a 1.5 million euro fine for market rigging in the 2005 attempted takeover of Antonveneta by Banca Popolare di Lodi, after prosecutors argued he had repeatedly favoured Fiorani's bank over ABN Amro by speeding some authorisations and slowing others.
n:BTG Pactual: BTG Pactual is a bank based in São Paulo, Brazil, tied to three central banks and one forum. On 3 October 2019 Brazil's Federal Police and the São Paulo federal prosecutors launched Operation Estrela Cadente into leaks of the Central Bank of Brazil's Copom interest-rate decisions in 2010, 2011 and 2012 to benefit a BTG Pactual fund, investigating passive and active corruption, use of inside information and money laundering; details remained under court seal and the allegations are unproven. Its other ties are careers. Guillermo Ortiz went from governor of the Bank of Mexico to chairman of BTG Pactual's Mexican business, and he represents the firm, as senior adviser and board member, in the Group of Thirty, a forum where central bankers and private financiers sit together, where he is also treasurer. Rodrigo Valdes was chief economist for the Andean region and Argentina at BTG Pactual and worked in the Central Bank of Chile's own research directorate before becoming Chile's Minister of Finance.
n:Barclays: Barclays is a bank based in London, United Kingdom, tied to three central banks. Most of the ties are careers at the Bank of England: David Roberts, Chair of its Court, came from executive and chair roles at Barclays, Lloyds Banking Group, Nationwide, Beazley and Bawag; Lord Jitesh Gadhia, a Non-Executive Director of the Court, from investment banking at Blackstone, Barclays Capital, ABN AMRO and Baring Brothers; and Katharine Braddick became Deputy Governor for Prudential Regulation on 1 July 2026 from the post of Barclays group head of strategic policy. Richard Fisher went the other way, from president and chief executive of the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas to senior adviser at Barclays from 1 July 2015, and Janet Yellen, Federal Reserve chair until early 2018, listed Barclays among the firms that paid her for speeches, pledging to seek written authorization before taking part in matters related to it. Rodrigo Valdes, once research director and chief economist of the Central Bank of Chile, was chief economist for Latin America at Barclays Capital. One record is a case: Hogg resigned as a Bank of England deputy governor on 14 March 2017 after the House of Commons Treasury Committee published a report finding that her failure, on multiple occasions since joining the Bank in 2013, to declare her brother's role as director of group strategy at Barclays was a 'very serious breach'; she said she had also unintentionally misled the committee.
n:Credit Suisse: Credit Suisse is a bank based in Zurich, Switzerland, tied to five central banks. Four of the ties are careers or paid work, not wrongdoing. Adachi Seiji, a member of the Bank of Japan's Policy Board from 2020, worked at Credit Suisse First Boston Securities (Japan) from 2001 before moving to Deutsche Securities and then Marusan Securities; Atsushi Mizuno left the same Policy Board to become vice chairman of fixed-income operations in Asia-Pacific at Credit Suisse. Ilan Goldfajn, governor of the Central Bank of Brazil from May 2016 to February 2019, held roles at Itaú Unibanco, Credit Suisse Brazil and the International Monetary Fund. Arjuna Mahendran was chief economist-strategist at Credit Suisse Private Bank before returning to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka, which he had joined as a staff officer in 1983, as its thirteenth Governor from January 2015 to June 2016. Janet Yellen, Federal Reserve chair until early 2018, was paid by Credit Suisse for speeches or advice and pledged to seek written authorization before taking part in matters related to it. The fifth tie is Mozambique's 'hidden debts' case. Letters from 2013 presented at a United States trial showed that the Bank of Mozambique had authorized Proindicus to seek a 372 million dollar Credit Suisse loan, later 622 million, and Ematum an 850 million dollar loan, part of more than 2 billion dollars of hidden debts owed to Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia. The letters were signed by board member Silvia de Abreu after a dispatch from governor Ernesto Gove, who in 2016 denied responsibility and said he had never heard of Proindicus. Testifying as a witness at the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021, in the trial of 19 people, Gove said he had signed authorisations for Proindicus, Ematum and MAM on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities in how the central bank granted them, including that the requests were handed personally to senior bank officials rather than submitted at a counter and that the financing contracts with Credit Suisse had already been signed; judge Efigenio Baptista rejected his argument that the foreign exchange rule barring such loans applied only to guarantees obtained after loans were agreed. A newssheet reported that Gove's status as a suspect had been confirmed and that he may face charges of abuse of office and membership of a criminal organisation; those charges are unproven.
n:BBVA: BBVA is a bank based in Bilbao, Spain, tied to four central banks through the careers of four people. José Manuel González-Páramo went from the European Central Bank's Executive Board to BBVA's. José Luis Escrivá was chief economist and General Director of Public Finances at BBVA Group, then held public posts, before becoming Governor of the Banco de España, Spain's central bank, from 2024. Joaquín Vial, chief economist of BBVA, became the government's nominee to the council of Chile's central bank in January 2012. Eduardo Torres-Llosa left the post of managing director of BBVA in Peru in June 2019 and became general manager of the Banco Central de Reserva del Peru in March 2022.
n:BNP Paribas: BNP Paribas is a bank based in Paris, France, tied to three central banks. Janet Yellen, chair of the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, until early 2018, listed BNP Paribas among the firms that paid her for speeches after she left; her disclosures, filed before her Treasury confirmation, showed more than 7 million dollars of speaking income in recent years. François Villeroy de Galhau was Chief Operating Officer of the BNP Paribas group before becoming Governor of the Banque de France, the French central bank, on 1 November 2015. Mohamed Lamine Lebbou worked at BNP Paribas El Djazaïr from 2004 to 2006, then headed the state-owned Banque nationale d'Algérie from 2021 to 2024 and BEA International Bank from May 2025, and was appointed Governor of the Banque d'Algérie in February 2026.
n:Bank of America: Bank of America is a bank based in Charlotte, United States, tied to three central banks, in each case through people. Two Federal Reserve governors are involved: Susan Schmidt Bies, a governor from 2001 to 2007, was elected to Bank of America's board of directors in 2009, and H. Robert Heller came from Bank of America to the Board of Governors from 19 August 1986 to 31 July 1989, going on to run Visa U.S.A. and then Fair Isaac Corporation. Janet Yellen, Fed chair until early 2018, was paid for speeches by financial firms named in her disclosures, which showed more than 7 million dollars of speaking income in recent years and among which Bank of America was named. Agus Martowardojo, elected Governor of Bank Indonesia in 2013 after serving as Minister of Finance and managing director of Bank Mandiri, held a post at Bank of America in 1984; no ethics finding is recorded. Yaseen Anwar worked at Bank of America from 1976 to 1991 and then at Merrill Lynch, before being appointed Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan on 29 March 2007 and Governor on 19 October 2011.
n:Swiss Re: Swiss Re is a company based in Zurich, Switzerland, tied to three central banks through the careers of three people. Roger W. Ferguson Jr., a governor of the Federal Reserve from 1997 and its vice chairman from October 1999 to April 2006, had been a McKinsey partner until 1987 and went on to the Swiss Re executive board and the chairmanship of Swiss Re America Holding Corporation, then to run TIAA-CREF. Sir Paul Tucker joined the Swiss Re board of directors after serving as Deputy Governor of the Bank of England, the United Kingdom's central bank, from 2009 to 2013. Jean-Pierre Roth, who joined the Swiss National Bank in 1979 and chaired its governing board from 2001 to 2009, also joined the Swiss Re board.
n:Bank for International Settlements: The Bank for International Settlements is a bank for central banks, based in Basel, Switzerland, and tied to 64 of them. Sixty-three central banks own it: its capital is held by central banks only, private shares having been bought back in 2001, and the owners run from the Federal Reserve System, the Bank of England, the Bank of France, the Deutsche Bundesbank and the European Central Bank to the People's Bank of China, the Bank of Japan, the Bank of Russia, the Reserve Bank of India, the Saudi Central Bank, the South African Reserve Bank and the Reserve Bank of Australia. It also holds gold for several central banks, which is custody rather than management. The Reserve Bank of India keeps part of India's gold in safe custody with the Bank of England and the Bank for International Settlements. The Bank of Portugal has 641,030 fine ounces there, about 5 per cent of its total. The National Bank of Belgium says a much smaller portion of its gold is held at the Bank for International Settlements and the Bank of Canada. The Bank of Japan's gold claims were moved, by a notice dating from 2000, out of a sight account and into an ear-marked account, meaning gold held for the depositor; the change was technical, with no new gold bought. The governor of Argentina's central bank, Santiago Bausili, told the Senate that part of its gold is deposited at the Bank for International Settlements in Switzerland, without attaching a tonnage to the location. The Central Bank of West African States keeps gold there as well, alongside its own head office and the Banque de France, put by Agence Ecofin at close to 106,000 ounces valued at 176.4 billion CFA francs and falling during 2024 as part of the gold was redeployed into placement operations; it has also bought units in an investment fund called BISIP K, managed by the Bank for International Settlements, worth 205,811 million CFA francs on 31 December 2025, down from 222,297 million a year earlier. One record is a career: Joachim Nagel, a Deutsche Bundesbank Executive Board member from 2010 to 2016 and its President since January 2022, moved to the KfW Executive Board and then to the Bank for International Settlements.
